finding: §2.1's third no-rows cause gives two contradictory answers for a line holding the JSON literal `null`, and the spec asserts they are the same rule. The stated predicate is "any non-blank line ... fails to parse as a JSON object" — `null` is not an object, so the round contributes no rows and every streak resets. The stated mechanism is "matching the audit record path, which unmarshals each line into a map and fails on anything else" — but Go's `json.Unmarshal([]byte("null"), &map[string]any{})` returns a nil error and a nil map, so that implementation accepts the line and yields a roleless, non-PASS row (verified: `null` err=nil, while `5`, `[]` and `"x"` all error). The two readings differ observably: discard-the-round resets `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` to null/0 and suppresses `divergence`; accept-the-row leaves the streak intact and adds 1 to `other_roles_open` and `unattributed_open`. §2.1 also asserts such a file "was truncated or hand-edited" because "--record ... rejects malformed rows" — that is false for this input: `countAuditFindings` unmarshals into a map, so a `null` line passes the record path and is counted as one finding, making the state reachable through the normal loop. Test 8's "a line holding a JSON scalar" and test 10's "a file holding a non-object line" are both unpinned on whether `null` is such a line.

finding: The roles_stale question raised in an earlier round was closed this revision by two new sentences whose stated ground is false against the code, in both halves. (a) §2.4 ends with "The corpus-staleness axis is left out for the same reason it is left in the payload: roles_stale is already reported beside the signal" and Non-Goal 14 repeats it as "roles_stale already reports that on --status beside the signal". engine.RolesStale (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:277-286) compares ONLY the latest recorded round's stored RolesHash against the current corpus hash, and recordAuditRoundEntry stamps each round with the corpus hash computed at record time (internal/cli/audit_record.go:106,125). So a corpus edited between two recorded rounds — the exact state Non-Goal 14 concedes ("A streak can span an auditor-corpus change") — leaves roles_stale FALSE at every later round. With rounds 1-3 on corpus A and rounds 4-9 on corpus B, spec_coverage_clean_rounds is 9, divergence fires, and the payload positively asserts roles_stale: false beside it. That is not silence about the instability, it is a false reassurance, and §1's invariant ("Every rule that could fail in two directions fails toward 'keep auditing'") is violated in the one direction §2.1 says is forbidden — the signal is made more likely to fire, not less. (b) The unqualified "already reported beside the signal" is also wrong on half the surface §2.5 names: runAuditRecord's payload (internal/cli/audit_record.go:74-97) carries converged, stale, harness_stale/harness_note and next_action, and no roles_stale key at all — Non-Goal 14's own "on --status" qualifier concedes this while §2.4's sentence does not.

finding: §2.1 closes its advisory table with "It applies on both outputs named in §2.5", i.e. the advisory must fire on `tp audit --status` and on `tp audit --record`. Test 8 ("The three no-rows causes each end every streak and emit their own advisory wording exactly once") names no output at all, and no other §6 item pins the advisory on `--record`. finding: §2.1's third bullet makes two claims that a bare `null` line makes mutually exclusive. It says a line parsing as a JSON scalar "is not an object and takes the same path as an unparseable one, matching the audit record path, which unmarshals each line into a map and fails on anything else", and then that "A recorded round is only reachable through --record, which rejects malformed rows, so a file in this state was truncated or hand-edited." In Go, json.Unmarshal of the literal `null` into a map[string]any succeeds and leaves the map nil, so countAuditFindings (internal/cli/audit_record.go:145-153) does NOT fail on it: it accepts the line, reads a missing status, counts it as a finding, and --record stores the file verbatim. A `null` row is therefore reachable in a recorded round with no hand editing, and the two rules disagree about it — strict "is a JSON object" makes the whole round contribute no rows (every streak reset, an "unparseable rows" advisory fired over a file tp itself accepted), while parity with the record path makes it an ordinary roleless non-PASS row. Test 8's "a line holding a JSON scalar" and test 10's non-object-line case inherit the same ambiguity depending on which scalar the implementer picks.

finding: `divergence.open_roles` and `divergence.unattributed_open` are pure arithmetic over two siblings that §2.5 guarantees are co-emitted on the very same two outputs and kept whole under `--compact`. `open_roles` is exactly {e.role | e in role_streaks, e.open > 0} minus `spec-coverage`, sorted by the byte order §2.2 already fixes — every role holding an open row in the latest round is by §2.2's own membership rule an entry of `role_streaks` with `open > 0`. `unattributed_open` is the latest round's total non-PASS count minus the sum of `role_streaks[].open`, since `role_streaks` covers every attributed role in that round; that total is always present and never stripped (`findings` in the base result map of runAuditRecord, `audit_rounds` in the base result map of runAuditStatus — internal/cli/audit_record.go L74-82 and L189-196, neither behind an IsCompact guard). §2.4 makes the co-presence argument explicitly for `other_roles_open` against `findings` (L114) but never makes it against `role_streaks`, and the ground it gives for `open_roles` — 'so the decision §2.6 hands to the driver can usually be made from `divergence` alone' — is empty when `role_streaks` can never be absent beside it. §2.5's own stated test for `--compact` ('drops what restates something already in the payload') therefore selects these two fields, yet §2.5 grants the keep-whole exception with a rationale that covers only `message`, `hint` and `role_streaks` by name.

finding: Whenever divergence is emitted, condition 2 makes the latest round unclean and condition 4 makes it non-converged, so AuditNextAction (internal/engine/nextaction.go:64-72) necessarily takes branch 2 and next_action reads "address the findings, then re-audit". The same payload therefore carries an unconditional directive to fix the findings beside divergence.hint saying the driver must "Decide explicitly whether they gate this release". §2.6 declares next_action unchanged and Non-Goal 4 declines a divergence branch, but neither section says which field a driver should act on — and next_action is the decision-critical field that survives --compact and that an agent driver reads first. §1's stated failure mode is precisely a driver acting on the shape tp prints; this release leaves the most-read field still printing the conclusion §1 calls wrong.

finding: `hint` is a compile-time constant (§2.6) and `message` varies only in three counts, and §2.5 pins both under `--compact` — but no section states what the signal costs in its steady state. `divergence` fires on every subsequent round for as long as its four conditions hold, and Non-Goal 8 removes any way for the driver to acknowledge it, so over the v0.32.0 history this release is built from the object would have fired on rounds 3 through 11: nine `--record` invocations plus every `--status --check` beside them, each carrying a byte-identical ~230-character `hint` whose information content after the first read is zero. §1's own diagnosis is that a signal repeated unchanged across eight rounds stops being read, so a spec that reasons this carefully about every other byte should say why this repetition escapes its own finding. The reason exists and the spec never gives it: under the reset-native subagent-per-unit model a round's driver may be a fresh context that has never seen the hint, so per-invocation self-sufficiency is a requirement rather than waste.

finding: Test 17's headline contradicts its own body, in the one place the release's newest rule is pinned. It reads "Condition 4 holds where conditions 1-3 do: with a task-file audit_clean_rounds of 0 reaching the resolver, so that converged is true ... divergence is absent". §2.4 fixes the technical sense of 'hold' for these conditions — 'divergence is emitted when all four hold', 'When any condition fails, divergence is absent' — and in this fixture condition 4 FAILS: converged is true, so 'the sequence is not converged' is false, which is precisely why divergence is absent. Read with §2.4's meaning the headline asserts the opposite of the fixture; read loosely ('condition 4 is what applies here') it is right, and nothing in the item distinguishes the readings.
